name: SwapX arbitrary transferFrom on approval holders
summary: SwapX exposes selector 0x4f1f05bc, which takes the token owner as a caller-supplied argument and runs transferFrom against it into a pair the caller also chooses, with no check that the owner is the caller. Every wallet that had ever approved SwapX could therefore be drained by anyone, and the attacker swept 68 of them in a single transaction and swapped the proceeds to WBNB.
notes: Non-upgradeable contract. The runtime code hash is 0x6088a520ddcc24072797530768424012b4fe19e4b09de3b48e3b18cfb63b604f both at the deployment block 12168762 and at block 26023088, and the EIP-1967 implementation slot is zero, so no code change occurred between deployment and the exploit.

The attacker pulled a long list of approval holders in two transactions and routed each balance straight through a PancakeSwap pair, so the tokens never sat in the attacker’s hands at a markable price. Netting both transactions across the attacker EOA and its exploit contract leaves 739.641476234907877084 WBNB gained and 1,000,000 DND of the attacker’s own token spent, so the realised proceeds are used as the measure rather than a mark on the drained tokens, which were mostly thin BSC assets sold into their own pools. Contemporaneous reporting put the event near USD 1 million on a nominal basis; that figure is not reproducible from the realised flows and is not used. Nothing was recovered.
